import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_10/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_10/training_1.csv"

Source5_10_0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
Source5_10_1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source5_10_0 and Source5_10_1 on "school_name"
joined_df = pd.merge(Source5_10_0, Source5_10_1, how="inner", on="school_name")

# Operation 2: group_by Source5_10_0.school_name and aggregate avg(Source5_10_0.reading_score)
# Note: After join, the reading_score column is from Source5_10_0, so it remains "reading_score"
# Group by "school_name" and calculate average reading_score
result_df = (
    joined_df.groupby("school_name", as_index=False)
    .agg({"reading_score": "mean"})
)

# Rename columns to match target schema explicitly (though names already match)
result_df = result_df.rename(columns={"school_name": "school_name", "reading_score": "reading_score"})

# Ensure data types match target schema: school_name as string, reading_score as float
result_df["school_name"] = result_df["school_name"].astype(str)
result_df["reading_score"] = result_df["reading_score"].astype(float)

# Write the result to the target CSV file
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_10/target_multisource.csv"
result_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
